text:
ana: kicking off capacity planning for next two quarters. need scenario runs for committed vs spot mix, region expansion windows, and safety stock for private deployments. can we sync tomorrow?

mike: +1. i'll pull last quarter utilization and per-model p99 token curves. any constraints from finance/product we should bake in?

sophia: customer asks are stacking: 1) EU private cluster for regulated fintech customer (target H2), 2) lower-latency NA nodes for conversational agents, 3) embed-heavy workloads spiking in PLG that need throughput. we should map to SLA tiers.

raja: budget note: Q3 commit envelope is fixed at $1.2M CAPEX equivalent. we can convert up to 20% to spot purchases.

elaine: vendor update: for A100-equivalent SKUs lead times are 10-14 weeks if we order today; for next-gen chips it's 18-26 weeks. spot/market availability varies week-to-week; ANZ/EU shipping has occasional 3-5 day delays at customs.

mike: rough scenarios (will refine):
```
Scenario A: conservative (70% committed, 30% spot) -> ensures headroom for H2 EU launch, higher cost
Scenario B: balanced (50/50) -> moderate cost, flexible scaling
Scenario C: aggressive spot (30% committed, 70% spot) -> lowest cost but higher risk during spikes
```

ana: @mike tiny typo: "ana" 🙂

ana: thanks — also add a "safety buffer" row for private deployments: +15% for reserved capacity to meet onboarding SLAs.

mike: noted. i'll run sims this afternoon and post projected p99 latency and cost per 1M requests for each scenario.

raja: also include downside case if a vendor pushes lead time +4 weeks. that impacts rollout gating for EU private.

elaine: flagged. pro tip: if you order as 'reserved capacity' we can negotiate a shorter lead with vendor rebate clauses. needs procurement sig.

deploy-bot: Reminder: quarterly capacity review meeting scheduled in #eng-infra for 2026-10-02 15:00 UTC (added by ana).

ana: action items: 1) @mike run sims + cost table, 2) @elaine check vendor rebate/leadtime options, 3) @raja model budget flex for +4 week lead, 4) @sophia map customer launch dates to each scenario. please drop updates in this thread by EOD tomorrow.

sophia: will align product launch calendar and flag must-have customers vs nice-to-have.

mike: posting interim numbers in 30m.

ana: thanks all. we'll decide procurement mix in the meeting taking into account safety buffer and SLA tiers. :thumbsup:
